---
title: "Exercise. The four dplyr verbs with the Latvian Labour Force Survey (solutions)"
format: html
---

Each part answers one question about work in Latvia in 2025. Codes are in `data/lfs_codebook.md`.

| Verb | What it does | Part |
|---|---|---|
| `filter()` | Extract specific observations (rows) | A |
| `select()` | Remove distracting columns | B |
| `mutate()` | Compute new variables | C |
| `summarise()` | Summarize cases | D |

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, here, janitor)
```

## Look first

```{r}
#| label: look
# One row per person. Blank cells mean "not applicable", "." is also read as missing
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  glimpse()
```

# Part A. filter(): extract rows

## A1. How many people are employed?

```{r}
#| label: a1
# EKA == 1 means employed. count() with no column counts rows.
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(EKA == 1) |>
  count()
```

## A2. How many employed women aged 25 to 54 live in the Riga region?

```{r}
#| label: a2
# Vecums 3, 4, 5 = ages 25 to 54. B11 == 2 = women. Jreg5 == 1 = Riga.
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(EKA == 1, B11 == 2, Vecums %in% 3:5, Jreg5 == 1) |>
  count()
```

## A3. Who works part time because no full-time job was available?

```{r}
#| label: a3
# D55 == 2 part time. D56 == 3 could not find full-time work.
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(D55 == 2, D56 == 3) |>
  select(NR, Vecums, B11, Jreg5, Stundas)
```

## A4. How many unemployed people have higher education?

```{r}
#| label: a4
# EKA == 2 unemployed. L124 == 1 higher education.
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(EKA == 2, L124 == 1) |>
  count()
```

## A5. Quality check: how many employed people have no answer on hours?

```{r}
#| label: a5
# Stundas == 9 is "no answer". is.na() catches blank cells.
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(EKA == 1) |>
  filter(Stundas == 9 | is.na(Stundas)) |>
  count()
```

# Part B. select(): remove distracting columns

## B1. Keep who the person is

```{r}
#| label: b1
# Four columns: ID, age group, sex, region
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(NR, Vecums, B11, Jreg5)
```

## B2. Which columns describe the household?

```{r}
#| label: b2
# starts_with() picks every column whose name begins with MS_
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(NR, starts_with("MS_"))
```

## B3. Drop the weights and give columns readable names

```{r}
#| label: b3
# -starts_with() removes columns. rename(new = old) changes names.
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(NR, Vecums, B11, Jreg5, EKA, Svars_G) |>
  rename(id = NR, age_group = Vecums, sex = B11, region = Jreg5, activity = EKA, weight = Svars_G)
```

## B4. Which columns have no values at all?

```{r}
#| label: b4
# where() selects columns by a test. Here: every value is missing.
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(where(\(x) all(is.na(x)))) |>
  names()
```

# Part C. mutate(): compute new variables

## C1. Is the annual weight one quarter of the quarterly weight?

```{r}
#| label: c1
# Arithmetic: divide one column by another
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(ratio = Svars_Cet / Svars_G) |>
  count(ratio)
```

## C2. Turn codes into labels

```{r}
#| label: c2
# case_when(): condition ~ value, one line per code
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    sex = case_when(
      B11 == 1 ~ "Men",
      B11 == 2 ~ "Women"
    ),
    region = case_when(
      Jreg5 == 1 ~ "Riga",
      Jreg5 == 2 ~ "Vidzeme",
      Jreg5 == 3 ~ "Kurzeme",
      Jreg5 == 4 ~ "Zemgale",
      Jreg5 == 5 ~ "Latgale"
    ),
    activity = case_when(
      EKA == 1 ~ "Employed",
      EKA == 2 ~ "Unemployed",
      EKA == 3 ~ "Inactive"
    )
  ) |>
  select(NR, sex, region, activity)
```

## C3. Group ages into three bands

```{r}
#| label: c3
# Vecums codes: 2 = 15-24, 3 to 5 = 25-54, 6 and 7 = 55-74
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    age_band = case_when(
      Vecums == 2 ~ "15-24",
      Vecums %in% 3:5 ~ "25-54",
      Vecums %in% 6:7 ~ "55-74",
      .default = "Other"
    )
  ) |>
  count(age_band)
```

## C4. Flag part-time work

```{r}
#| label: c4
# A comparison returns TRUE or FALSE. Use it as a new column.
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(EKA == 1) |>
  mutate(part_time = D55 == 2) |>
  count(part_time)
```

# Part D. summarise(): summarize cases

The survey covers a sample. Each person has a weight (`Svars_G`), the number of people in Latvia that person stands for. Sum the weights to estimate people in Latvia. Use `Svars_G` for one year of data.

## D1. How many people aged 15 to 74 are employed, unemployed or inactive?

```{r}
#| label: d1
# count(wt = ...) adds up the weights instead of counting rows
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(!is.na(EKA)) |>
  mutate(
    activity = case_when(
      EKA == 1 ~ "Employed",
      EKA == 2 ~ "Unemployed",
      EKA == 3 ~ "Inactive"
    )
  ) |>
  count(activity, wt = Svars_G, sort = TRUE)
```

## D2. Which region has the highest share of employed people?

```{r}
#| label: d2
# Share = weighted employed / weighted total, by region
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(!is.na(EKA)) |>
  mutate(
    employed = EKA == 1,
    region = case_when(
      Jreg5 == 1 ~ "Riga",
      Jreg5 == 2 ~ "Vidzeme",
      Jreg5 == 3 ~ "Kurzeme",
      Jreg5 == 4 ~ "Zemgale",
      Jreg5 == 5 ~ "Latgale"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(employed_share = sum(Svars_G * employed) / sum(Svars_G)) |>
  arrange(desc(employed_share))
```

## D3. Do men or women work part time more often?

```{r}
#| label: d3
# Among employed people only
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(EKA == 1, D55 %in% 1:2) |>
  mutate(
    part_time = D55 == 2,
    sex = case_when(B11 == 1 ~ "Men", B11 == 2 ~ "Women")
  ) |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  summarise(part_time_share = sum(Svars_G * part_time) / sum(Svars_G))
```

## D4. In which sectors do women hold most jobs?

```{r}
#| label: d4
# Women's share of employed people, by sector of the main job
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(EKA == 1, D47 != 99) |>
  mutate(
    women = B11 == 2,
    sector = case_when(
      D47 == 1 ~ "Agriculture",
      D47 == 2 ~ "Industry and energy",
      D47 == 3 ~ "Construction",
      D47 == 4 ~ "Trade, accommodation, food",
      D47 == 5 ~ "Transport and ICT",
      D47 == 6 ~ "Finance and professional",
      D47 == 7 ~ "Public administration",
      D47 == 8 ~ "Education",
      D47 == 9 ~ "Health and social care",
      D47 == 10 ~ "Other"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(sector) |>
  summarise(women_share = sum(Svars_G * women) / sum(Svars_G)) |>
  arrange(desc(women_share))
```

## D5. Draw the answer to D4

```{r}
#| label: d5
#| fig-height: 4
# Show: sorted bars. Focus: one color. Tell: the title states the finding.
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(EKA == 1, D47 != 99) |>
  mutate(
    women = B11 == 2,
    sector = case_when(
      D47 == 1 ~ "Agriculture",
      D47 == 2 ~ "Industry and energy",
      D47 == 3 ~ "Construction",
      D47 == 4 ~ "Trade, accommodation, food",
      D47 == 5 ~ "Transport and ICT",
      D47 == 6 ~ "Finance and professional",
      D47 == 7 ~ "Public administration",
      D47 == 8 ~ "Education",
      D47 == 9 ~ "Health and social care",
      D47 == 10 ~ "Other"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(sector) |>
  summarise(women_share = sum(Svars_G * women) / sum(Svars_G)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = women_share, y = fct_reorder(sector, women_share))) +
  geom_col(fill = "gray40") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Women hold [DATA NEEDED HERE] of jobs in education",
    x = "Share of employed people who are women",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Source: Central Statistical Bureau of Latvia, Labour Force Survey 2025"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
